title: Comparative Advantage and Trade
text: Comparative advantage is the economic principle that countries or agents should specialize in producing goods where they have the lowest opportunity cost, and trade for other goods. It was formalized by David Ricardo in his 1817 work Principles of Political Economy, and differs from absolute advantage, where one party is simply better at producing everything. Even if one country is more efficient at producing all goods, mutually beneficial trade is still possible if each country specializes in its area of comparative advantage. This principle forms the theoretical foundation for free trade and arguments against protectionism. Empirical evidence generally supports the gains from trade predicted by comparative advantage.
